description:
Music to Calm Anxiety | Slow Bansuri | Indian Classical

Some stress doesn't wait for the weekend to end. It just follows you.

You're not at work. There's nothing urgent. But the body is still tense, the mind still running its loops, the background hum of anxiety still present even though the day is technically over. You can't force it to stop. You just need something to sit with while it slowly releases.

This is 90 minutes of slow Bansuri in Raga Yaman — the classical Indian evening raga. Yaman is expansive and open. Its raised fourth interval gives it an upward, outward quality — phrases that open instead of close, that ease instead of settle. It doesn't try to sedate. It just makes space.

The bamboo flute carries it with the warmth of breath. No percussion, no rhythm to track. Just sound that gradually changes the texture of the evening.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Bansuri — warm bamboo flute, breath-driven and slow
- Raga Yaman — the classical Indian evening raga, expansive and open
- Long sustained phrases with natural silences between them
- No percussion, no tabla — space to breathe
- A gentle theta layer barely audible underneath
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Still running
20:00   Beginning to slow
45:00   Tension releasing
70:00   Quiet
85:00   Still

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Don't try to relax — just let it be on. The Bansuri does the work. You just need to be in the room with it. By the time you notice it's working, it already has been for a while.

⏱ Best for:
• Anxiety that won't switch off in the evening
• Stress still running after work
• Restless Saturday or Sunday evenings
• Background for winding down
• Quiet company when the mind is too loud

production_spec.notes: Raga Yaman — classical Indian evening raga. Sa Re Ga Ma(teevra) Pa Dha Ni Sa. The raised 4th (teevra Ma) is Yaman's defining characteristic — gives it the expansive, open, upward quality distinct from heavier evening ragas. NOT Darbari (heavy, midnight) — Yaman is lighter and more spacious. LUFS -14 (evening viewer, awake and present — not sleep). Theta 5Hz for anxiety relief and mental calm (not Delta — viewer is not sleeping). No tabla — anxiety content needs space, rhythm would create unwanted energy. Bansuri mid-to-low register — high register is alerting, not calming. EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'evening giving anxiety somewhere to go' · clip 2: 'stress losing its grip — still and open' · clip 3: 'warm and present, held without pressure'. 90min = 3-4 Suno clips + loop extension.
